column1: # Batch 31 — rules 4 and 4b, the measurement CLAUDE.md asked for. 2026-10-11.
# tools/audit_batch_emit.py against the 16 reconstructed manifests, which is
# the tool that supplies each row's PROBE ENTITY. That matters: these are
# on-demand entity pivots, and audit_registry_emit.py (the registry sweep) runs
# every row with no entity, so it reported 268 of 295 as EMITS_NOTHING --
# a verdict about sources that had never been asked anything. The engine
# returned silently in that case, giving the sweep's own NEEDS_ENTITY verdict
# nothing to match on; it now says so, and the sweep recognises it.
# Of the 360 manifest rows, 65 are UNREGISTERED and that is the expected
# number: they are exactly the 65 FILTER_IGNORED rows removed on 2026-10-06
# (docs/probe-sources-batch31.tsv). The manifest is the probe record and the C
# is the maintained copy, so a removed row stays in the manifest and reads as
# unregistered here. The match being exact is also the proof that the removal
# The 295 live rows: 53 OK -- they fetch and store real records for their probe
# entity. 99 EMPTY_UPSTREAM, which is NOT the same as broken: the endpoint
# answered and held no record for that particular entity. 48 answered 404,
# 42 answered 403 and 37 failed at the transport level.
# Nothing is removed on this reading. One probe is one reading, 403 and 404 can
# be a user-agent or a host having a bad afternoon, and since 2026-10-06 each
# of these rows files a collector-fetch-failure record naming its status, so a
# refused fetch is legible in the data instead of being inferred from a TSV.
